clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old woman presented with severe intermittent headache, blurred vision, left hand numbness, night sweating, fatigue, muscular pain, and acute neuropsychiatric symptoms including agitation, behavioral changes, confusion, disorientation, and amnesia. Initial CSF analysis revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal protein and elevated glucose, negative gram stain and culture, and no malignant cells. Brain MRI was normal without inflammation or granulomas. Serum Brucella antibodies were positive at high titers (abortus 1:640, melitensis 1:160), indicating systemic Brucella infection. The patient was treated with Rifampicin, Doxycycline, and Moxifloxacin. Follow-up CSF analysis after one month normalized cell counts, and the patient showed significant symptomatic improvement after completing antibiotic therapy, supporting the diagnosis of neurobrucellosis with neuropsychiatric manifestations.
